title: LogSuite
headline: Seven offline-first productivity modules on one SQLite database
lede: Between June and November 2026, I built [LogSuite](https://github.com/aminurislamarnob/logsuite), an offline-first Flutter app that combines tasks, notes, habits, medicine schedules, expenses, a focus timer, and a quick-capture inbox called Drop. Every module reads and writes a local SQLite database through Drift and can be turned off in Settings when a user wants a smaller app. I made **all 102 non-merge commits** on `main`, pairing with Claude Code across 76 of them, and backed the codebase with 392 automated tests.

sections.heading: What the five months looked like

blocks.text: Most of the work landed in three stretches. Over 29 and 30 July (19 commits), I built the initial six-module app and migrated every screen from Material 3 widgets onto `forui` primitives. Between 2 and 13 September (69 commits), I rebuilt the expense module around people, loans, and monthly budgets, added the four-provider AI voice and document-scanning assistant, synthesised the six WAV ambient loops, and shipped full JSON backup and restore. On 5 and 6 November (11 commits), I built the Drop capture and triage module with tag suggestions, gamification, haptics, and an in-app browser. The repository was quiet from 25 June to 28 July, from 31 July to 1 September, and from 14 September to 28 October.

sections.heading: What had to be true from the start

blocks.text: From the README and taste rules, five constraints shaped the project:

items: **Offline-first persistence:** Every module reads and writes a local SQLite database through Drift (`lib/core/database/app_database.dart`), with no mandatory account or server.
**Optional modules:** Each module can be switched on or off in Settings so the navigation shell and dashboard only show what the user uses.
**First-class Bangladesh locale:** ৳ (BDT) currency, Bangla numerals (`০` to `৯`), seeded Cash, bKash, Nagad, and Bank accounts, and English/Bangla/Banglish voice parsing.

**User-owned AI keys:** Spoken and scanned commands work with Claude, OpenAI, Gemini, or DeepSeek using an API key kept in the platform keychain, and fall back to an offline parser when no key is set.
**No dead buttons or half-shipped features:** Every toggle, backup action, reminder, and sound option in the UI is wired end to end and covered by tests.

sections.heading: One SQLite database beneath seven modules

blocks.text: The UI sits on `go_router` nested shells and a shared widget kit in `lib/core/widgets/` built over `forui` primitives. `AppColors` defines the coral brand accent (`#F15F43`), a three-way pastel card rotation, and warm per-module tints that pass contrast checks.

Below the screens, Riverpod providers watch 22 Drift SQLite tables (`Folders`, `Notes`, `Tags`, `NoteTags`, `Projects`, `Tasks`, `TaskTags`, `Habits`, `HabitLogs`, `People`, `Medicines`, `MedicineDoses`, `SymptomLogs`, `Accounts`, `ExpenseCategories`, `Expenses`, `Budgets`, `RecurringExpenses`, `Loans`, `FocusSessions`, `Drops`, and `DropTags`). The AI command executor and the editor sheets write through the same repository methods, so a spoken or scanned entry produces the exact same rows and OS notifications as a typed one.

blocks.caption: ForUI screens watch Riverpod providers backed by 22 Drift SQLite tables, while the AI assistant reads API keys from the platform keychain.

sections.heading: Expenses: people, loans, and month-scoped budgets

blocks.text: Household spending rarely belongs to one person or stays inside simple income and expense rows. On 3 September I wrote `expense-module-plan.md` and shipped a 14-commit sequence (`0465f94` to `46cafbf`) that split `expenses_screen.dart` into five tab files (Overview, Reports, Budgets, Bills, and Loans) and added a core `People` table, month-scoped budgets, and a loan ledger.

Editing a transaction reverses its old account delta and applies the new one inside a single Drift transaction (`ead7675`). Swiping to delete raises an undo toast that re-inserts the row with its original primary key so `loanId` and receipt links stay intact. Deleting a category or person with history prompts to reassign those transactions rather than orphaning them.

sections.heading: Spoken sentences and scanned documents become previewed drafts

blocks.text: Between 5 and 8 September (`c77c448` to `fae2ac5`), and in PR #3 on 13 September (`9483453`), I built the AI assistant so a single sentence such as *'spent 200 taka on lunch with bKash and remind me to call the doctor at 5, and add Napa 3 times a day for 5 days'* creates an expense, a task with a reminder, and a medicine course.

Speech recognition and ML Kit document OCR always run on the device (`speech_service.dart`, `ocr_service.dart`), so audio and photos never leave the phone. The transcript is sent with the action schema (`ai_command_schema.dart`) and the names of the user's categories, accounts, people, habits, and projects to whichever provider is chosen in Settings: Claude, OpenAI, Gemini, or DeepSeek. The user's API key lives in `flutter_secure_storage` (platform keychain). Without a key, `LocalCommandParser` splits clauses on English and Banglish conjunctions (`and`, `then`, `ar`, `ebong`) and routes each clause to the local task, medicine, and expense parsers.

blocks.caption: On-device speech or OCR text is paired with local entity names, parsed into drafts, and shown as preview cards before any row is written.

sections.heading: Click-free WAV loops, all-or-nothing restore, and iOS motion

blocks.text: Three commits in early September closed gaps between what the UI offered and what ran underneath, followed by a full spacing and motion pass in PR #4 (`8665585`) and the rename from mySuite to LogSuite (`caa068b`).

items: Synthesised WAV loops (15cfc3d)

Six 16-bit mono PCM files in assets/sounds/ (rain, ocean, forest, cafe, white_noise, brown_noise) built in the frequency domain with random phase so every buffer is periodic and loops without an MP3/AAC padding click.
All-or-nothing JSON restore (15cfc3d)

RestoreService parses and validates the entire backup file before opening a database transaction, defers foreign keys for self-referencing folders, and decodes base64 profile photos back to local storage.
How-to guides (7f93da7)
Settings -> How to renders collapsible step-by-step cards from how_to_content.dart with a button that opens or enables each module.
Spacing and iOS motion (PR #4)
Unified AppSpacing tokens (gutter 20, section 24, card gap 10), computed bottom clearance from bar height plus safe-area inset, and added Cupertino swipe-back transitions and rubber-band overscroll.

sections.heading: Drop: quick-capture inbox, tag autocomplete, and triage gamification

blocks.text: On 29 October I added native Flutter integration tests (`integration_test/app_test.dart`, commit `acfef31`). Then on 5 and 6 November I shipped the seventh module, Drop (`2ee5f96` to `3953c20`, closing issues #5 through #13): a stream for capturing links, YouTube videos, photos, and rough thoughts before deciding where they belong.

items: **Rich capture and OS share sheet (#6, #7, #8, #11):** Schema v3 migration adds `Drops` and `DropTags`, ingests payloads from the native OS share sheet (`receive_sharing_intent`), scrapes OpenGraph and YouTube metadata for preview cards, downscales thumbnails to 400px, and runs on-device ML Kit OCR on images.

**Triage, escalation, and summarization (#9, #12, #13):** Items can be pinned, bulk-selected, scheduled with 'Remind Me Later' notifications, summarized with AI or extractive fallback, or converted into a Note or Task prefilled in its editor.
**WhatsApp-style `#` tag suggestions (`8ffdb49`, `9c9f698`):** Typing `#` in the bottom capture bar opens a suggestion card with fuzzy matching over existing tags.

**Gamification, haptics, and in-app browser (`1dd6ef8`, `4d05d73`, `3953c20`):** Triage actions award XP, build daily streaks, unlock badges, and trigger an Inbox Zero celebration, paired with an app-wide haptics toggle and an in-app browser with external launch fallback.

sections.heading: The details a visitor never sees

items: Restore table guard
restore_service_test.dart asserts that RestoreService.sections covers every table declared on AppDatabase, so a new table cannot be wiped and left empty on restore.
Audio seam test
ambient_sounds_test.dart parses the bundled WAV headers and samples to verify 16-bit mono PCM, matched RMS loudness, no clipping, and a wrap-around step no larger than interior sample steps.
Keychain storage
API keys use flutter_secure_storage across Android, iOS, macOS, and Linux (libsecret-1-dev), never SharedPreferences.
Git blame hygiene
Commit ee3f38b reformatted 911 lines across 22 files; commit 1d361c5 recorded it in .git-blame-ignore-revs so git blame still points to the commit that wrote the logic.

sections.heading: How I worked with Claude Code

blocks.text: I worked solo on the repository with Claude Code as my pair. For major changes such as the six-phase `forui` migration, the expense and loan schema (`expense-module-plan.md`), and the 9-issue Drop rollout, we agreed on the table shapes and commit order first, then landed small commits checked by in-memory Drift repository tests and widget tests.

blocks.text: LogSuite is at version `0.0.2+2` on [github.com/aminurislamarnob/logsuite](https://github.com/aminurislamarnob/logsuite), with native targets configured for Android, iOS, macOS, Linux, and Windows.

items: **7 toggleable modules** sharing one 22-table Drift SQLite database: Tasks, Notes, Habits, Medicine, Expenses, Focus, and Drop.
**4 AI providers plus offline fallback** turning spoken English, Bangla, or Banglish commands and scanned documents into previewed entries.
**392 passing automated tests** across 46 test files, plus native end-to-end coverage in `integration_test/app_test.dart`.

Eleven commits created inside my Claude Code sessions on 5 to 7 September carry `Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>` as the git author and count as mine; 76 of the 102 non-merge commits carry a `Co-Authored-By: Claude` trailer.
